summary: Targeted five claims: (1) 'no faith-specific leader-first precedent found' — the core open question, answered only via non-faith analogs; (2) the 'defer campus-ministry coalitions' recommendation, which the brief itself flagged as resting on absence-of-precedent rather than documented failure; (3) the carried-forward 'relational beats digital' premise in campus ministry, which has only practitioner-opinion corroboration despite being treated as settled across two research tasks; (4) the EdTech/Notion leader-first analog being adopted as the primary transferable pattern despite unexamined doctrinal-safety/trust friction; and (5) the diocese/parish material's UK/GDPR-only, compliance-only framing, untested against possible US-context persuasion-oriented material. All five are load-bearing for the brief's central recommendations and were selected for thin corroboration or overconfident restatement relative to sourcing, not personal disagreement with the brief.
